learning_plan.execution_strategy_summary: Alright, future Backend Developer! This isn't just a plan; it's *your* personalized weapon to conquer the startup tech scene. We're leveraging your strong academic CS foundation, your existing familiarity with C#, .NET, and even other backend frameworks, to build a razor-sharp C#/.NET Core profile. By focusing intensely on a single, continuously evolving Capstone project deployed to the cloud, you’ll not only master industry-grade skills but also craft an irresistible portfolio that screams 'production-ready' to any hiring manager. Your previous internships and academic projects mean you're not starting from zero; we're taking that foundation and supercharging it into an unfair advantage.

monthly_plan.theme: The C# Deep Dive & Professional Git Foundations
weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: You'll kick things off by elevating your C# skills, diving into modern features like pattern matching and records. We'll refresh advanced OOP (SOLID principles) and start applying them to clean up your existing C# codebases, transforming them from academic to production-ready.

Week 2: This week, we'll conquer asynchronous programming with `async/await` and the Task Parallel Library in C#. You’ll refactor those blocking I/O operations from Week 1 to be blazing fast, ensuring your code is responsive and efficient. Concurrently, you’ll start your professional Git journey by mastering advanced commands like rebase and cherry-pick.

Week 3: Time to solidify your C# expertise with Generics, Collections, and LINQ mastery, which are critical for writing concise and powerful data manipulation code. Simultaneously, you’ll immerse yourself in collaborative Git workflows, practicing branching strategies like GitFlow and GitHub Flow, and engaging in mock code reviews.

Week 4: We'll wrap up the C# deep dive by refining exception handling best practices and ensuring robust code. Crucially, you'll apply all your new Git knowledge by participating in a simulated open-source scenario, handling complex merge conflicts, and working with forks. This sets the stage for collaborative project work, an essential startup skill.

monthly_plan.theme: Database Design & Your First API Endpoints
weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: You'll dive deep into relational database theory, mastering normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF). This isn't just theory; you'll apply it immediately to design a robust database schema for our 'Task Management' Capstone, moving beyond generic database concepts from your CSE degree.

Week 2: Time to get hands-on with MySQL! You'll install it, configure it, and get comfortable with its command-line interface. You’ll then implement your 'Task Management' database schema, create tables, and populate it with initial seed data, gaining practical expertise with a prevalent database in startups.

Week 3: This week is all about advanced SQL. You'll master complex JOINs, subqueries, and even start exploring powerful window functions – skills crucial for extracting real business insights. You’ll write queries to fetch various statistics from your 'Task Management' data.

Week 4: We'll transition into API development with ASP.NET Core! You'll grasp the core architecture of Web APIs (controllers, routes, middleware) and start building your first RESTful endpoints (GET for all tasks, GET for a single task) for the 'Task Management' Capstone. You'll use Postman to test these endpoints rigorously, building on your existing conceptual understanding from Node.js/Express.js/PHP.

weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: You'll expand your 'Task Management' API to include POST endpoints for creating new tasks and users. This means implementing input validation to ensure data integrity – a crucial step for production APIs. You’ll master Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) for clean request/response handling.

Week 2: Now we tackle updating and deleting data. You'll implement PUT, PATCH, and DELETE endpoints for your 'Task Management' API, ensuring you have full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) capability. We'll also cover error handling best practices and custom exception middleware for graceful API responses.

Week 3: Time to introduce Entity Framework Core, the industry-standard ORM for .NET! You'll learn the benefits of ORMs, the Code-First approach, and how to manage your database schema using EF Core Migrations. You'll start integrating EF Core into your API for basic data operations.

Week 4: You'll replace all direct SQL calls in your 'Task Management' API with EF Core, mastering CRUD operations, and working with relationships (one-to-many, many-to-many) between your task and user entities. We'll also dive into asynchronous data access with EF Core and explore initial performance considerations like eager loading, leveraging your SQL knowledge and .NET Core API skills for streamlined database interactions.

monthly_plan.theme: Secure Your API & Master Quality Assurance
weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: Security is paramount! You'll learn the difference between authentication and authorization. We'll implement user registration and login endpoints for your 'Task Management' API, focusing on secure password hashing and storage practices.

Week 2: This week, you'll integrate JWT (JSON Web Tokens) authentication into your ASP.NET Core API. This is a non-negotiable skill for modern backend developers. You'll ensure secure token generation, validation, and usage across your API.

Week 3: Authorization takes center stage. You'll implement role-based and policy-based authorization to restrict access to specific API endpoints or even individual data (e.g., users can only modify their own tasks, admins can delete anything). This adds a crucial layer of security to your 'Task Management' system, applying your theoretical CS security knowledge directly to API development.

Week 4: Quality is built-in, not bolted on. You'll be introduced to Unit Testing principles, learn to use xUnit (or NUnit) with Moq for mocking dependencies, and start writing comprehensive unit tests for your 'Task Management' API's core business logic (services, controllers). We'll even touch upon the TDD (Test-Driven Development) workflow for one new feature, moving you from academic coding to professional development with reliable, maintainable code.

weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: Modern deployment starts with Docker. You'll learn containerization fundamentals (images, containers, volumes) and write your first Dockerfiles for your 'Task Management' .NET Core API. This makes your application portable and consistent across environments, building on your existing backend projects.

Week 2: You'll take containerization to the next level by using Docker Compose to orchestrate both your .NET Core API and its MySQL database as a single, multi-container application. This allows for easy local development and consistent deployment environments.

Week 3: Time to go to the cloud! You'll get an introduction to Azure fundamentals, setting up an Azure App Service for Containers or Azure Container Apps. You'll then deploy your Dockerized 'Task Management' application to Azure, making it accessible to the world, providing a full-circle view of the software delivery lifecycle.

Week 4: We'll complete the deployment cycle with CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment). You'll set up a GitHub Actions workflow to automatically build, test, Dockerize, and deploy your 'Task Management' API to Azure whenever you push changes to your main branch. This automation is a huge hiring signal! We'll also introduce Microservices architecture concepts to give you a foundational understanding of scalable systems, preparing you for advanced challenges in startup jobs.

critical_guidelines: **Embrace the 70/30 Rule, Relentlessly:** You have 3 hours a day, so 70% of that time (2.1 hours) MUST be hands-on coding, debugging, or building. The other 30% (0.9 hours) is for reading, watching, and planning. Stick to this like glue; it's your shield against tutorial hell and ensures you're actively building the muscle memory for a production-ready role.

**Time-Box Your Struggles:** When you hit a bug or a concept that just won't click, set a timer for 30-45 minutes. If you're still stuck, STOP. Take a break, rubber duck it, ask for help from online communities, or research. Do NOT spend hours banging your head against a wall – your time is precious, and knowing when to seek help is a critical professional skill.

**The Capstone is Your Core:** Every module, every exercise, should feed into your 'Task Management' Capstone project. It's your living resume. Make it the best thing you've ever built, continually adding features and layers of complexity as you learn new skills. This project, with its end-to-end execution and deployment, *will* get you hired; treat it as your most important asset.

**Prioritize Interview Prep Early & Consistently:** Don't wait until the last month to cram DS&A or System Design. Dedicate focused time each week, starting from Month 1. Consistent practice over time builds muscle memory and confidence, which is critical under interview pressure – it’s a marathon, not a sprint.

**Ask for Help, Build Your Network:** You are not alone on this journey. Leverage online communities (Stack Overflow, Discord, Reddit's r/csharp), reach out to mentors (if you have them), and don't be afraid to connect with people on LinkedIn, especially those in startups using C#/.NET. The tech community thrives on shared knowledge; become a proactive part of it.

You've transformed your academic background and existing familiarity with C#, .NET, and other backend frameworks into a powerful, production-ready C#/.NET Core backend developer profile. Your comprehensive 'Task Management' Capstone project, fully developed, securely tested, containerized, and deployed live on Azure with a CI/CD pipeline, will stand as undeniable proof of your capabilities. Recruiters will see a candidate who not only understands the 'what' but has rigorously executed the 'how' – someone who can hit the ground running, build robust solutions, adapt to startup environments, and actively contribute to a team's success. You're not just ready; you're ready to code, create, and confidently conquer your first industry role!
